scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Bulba was choreographed by Igor Moiseyev following a visit to Belarus in the late 1930s.
Drawing on traditional Belarusian folklore and an overheard folk song of the same name, Moiseyev crafted a concert piece that entered the repertory of regional ensembles.

When he returned to Belarus fifteen years later, he discovered the dance was performed across the country, with locals asserting it had always existed despite folklorists confirming its origin in Moiseyev's choreography.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The work humorously portrays the agricultural cycle of potato production.
The word 'bulba' means potato in Belarusian and Ukrainian, reflecting a central staple of local life.
Moiseyev regarded its universal adoption into Belarusian national repertoire as the highest form of recognition.
Today it is a living tradition.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Bulba (Belarus). Vocal style: Belarusian folk song with humorous portrayal. Mood: vivid, humorous, lively. The music supports a comedic theatrical narrative portraying agricultural work. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
